Definition: from G3844 and G2983; to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation); by analogy, to assume an office; figuratively, to learn:--receive, take (unto, with).
BiblicalUsage: Paralambanō is to take to oneself, to receive, to take along. Joseph is told, Fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife; Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up into a high mountain; He promises, I will come again, and receive you unto Myself; and Paul says, I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe receiving is the shape of the Christian life. Joseph receives Mary, the three receive the vision, we are received by Christ, and Paul receives the supper to hand it on.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary; Paul
